name: Erne

attributes.attribute: chief among the maidens of Cruachan

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Vol. III. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, 461–467.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Erne was an Irish heroine or goddess. The dindshenchas, Ireland's place-name poetry, records her story. This poetry explains how the River Erne and its rising lake gained their names. A noblewoman named Erne was chief among the maidens of Cruachan. Cruachan was the capital of Connacht. A giant voice roared from the opening of Oweynagat, the Cave of the Cats. It frightened her and her women away from home. Erne took the comb of her mistress, the queen Medb. The comb symbolized feminine potency. She led her party north to a lake, and they all drowned. A woman drowned in a great water-source marks an ancient watershed goddess.
